conversations.subject: Dashboard loading extremely slowly after recent update

comments.author: customer
comments.content: After upgrading to the newest version (v4.2.1) of your software yesterday, our main dashboard is taking over 30 seconds to load. This is causing significant delays for our team as we need to access this dashboard constantly throughout the day. The previous version was working fine with load times of ~2 seconds. Can you please help us resolve this issue ASAP? We have already tried clearing the browser cache and restarting the application.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Hi there, thank you for bringing this issue to our attention. I'm sorry to hear about the slow dashboard loading time you're experiencing. To help troubleshoot, could you please provide some additional information?

1. What browser and version are you using?
2. How many widgets do you have configured on your dashboard?
3. Are you seeing any specific error messages in the browser console?
4. Is this happening for all users or just specific team members?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: We're using Chrome 114.0.5735.198 and Firefox 115.0.2 - the issue occurs in both browsers. We have about 12 widgets on the dashboard, which is the same setup we had before the update. No error messages in the console, just extremely slow loading. It's happening for everyone on our team (15 users total). We've also tried accessing from different locations/networks, and the problem persists.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've shared, this sounds like it might be related to a known performance issue with the latest update when handling dashboards with multiple data-intensive widgets. I'd like to try a few things:

1. Could you navigate to Settings > Performance and temporarily change the 'Data Refresh Rate' from 'Real-time' to 'Every 5 minutes'?

2. If that doesn't help, could you try disabling the 'Advanced Analytics' widget temporarily to see if that improves loading times?

Let me know if either of these steps makes a difference, and I'll continue working on a more permanent solution.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: I changed the refresh rate setting as suggested, but it only improved the loading time to about 20 seconds, which is still far too slow. Then I disabled the Advanced Analytics widget, and that got us to about 15 seconds, but that's a widget we absolutely need for our operations. This is really impacting our productivity - we have deadlines to meet and can't afford to waste time waiting for the dashboard to load every time we need to check something. Is there any way to revert to the previous version until this is fixed?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I understand your frustration, and appreciate your patience as we work through this. The performance impact is more significant than we initially thought. Let me investigate downgrade options.

In the meantime, I've escalated this to our development team as a high priority issue. They've identified a potential cause related to a new data processing algorithm in the Advanced Analytics widget that becomes inefficient with larger datasets.

Could you please tell me approximately how many data points you're tracking in the Advanced Analytics widget? Also, would you be willing to allow our team to access your dashboard remotely to collect diagnostic information? This would help us develop a fix more quickly.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: We're tracking about 5,000 data points in the Advanced Analytics widget across 3 different data sources. This is really unacceptable - we weren't notified that the update would cause such significant performance issues. We've now lost almost a full day of productivity across the team. I'd really prefer to just roll back to the previous version immediately rather than continue troubleshooting. If remote access is the only way to resolve this, I need to get approval from our security team, which will take at least another day.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I completely understand your frustration, and I apologize for the disruption this has caused to your team's workflow. You're right that this situation is not acceptable.

Good news - I've just spoken with our technical team, and I can help you downgrade to the previous version (v4.1.9) immediately. Here's how we can proceed:

1. Please go to Settings > System > Version Control
2. Select "Restore Previous Version" from the dropdown
3. Confirm when prompted

This will restore your system to v4.1.9 without affecting any of your data or dashboard configurations. The process should take about 5 minutes to complete.

Additionally, I've added your account to our priority notification list, so you'll receive advance warning about any potential issues with future updates. Our development team is already working on a patch for this issue, which we expect to release within the next 48 hours.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: I've followed your instructions and downgraded to v4.1.9. The dashboard is now loading in 2-3 seconds again, so we're back to normal operation. I appreciate the quick resolution, but I'm still concerned about the update process. We can't afford this kind of disruption again. Will the next update definitely fix this issue without introducing new problems? And will we be able to test it in a non-production environment first? I need some assurance before we consider upgrading again.

You're welcome! I'm glad we could resolve this to your satisfaction. The corrected invoice will be issued within the next 24 hours, and you'll receive an email notification when it's available in your billing portal.

Absolutely - you can verify your billable user count at any time by logging into your admin dashboard and navigating to Settings > Account > Billing Summary. This page shows your current billable user count in real-time. I recommend checking this a few days before the end of each billing cycle.

Additionally, I'm setting up a monthly automated billing summary email for your account that will be sent to you 5 days before each billing cycle ends. This will give you time to review and reach out if you notice any discrepancies.

I think this covers everything for now. I'll be on the lookout for the corrected invoice and will check the credits on our next statement.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Perfect! The monthly summary email has been set up, and you'll receive your first one next month. I've also made a note in your account about our conversation today and the resolution we've provided.

I want to personally apologize again for the inconvenience this billing issue has caused. We take these matters seriously and are implementing additional checks in our billing system to prevent similar errors in the future.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions when you receive the corrected invoice or if you need assistance with anything else. Your satisfaction is our priority, and we're grateful for your business.

conversations.subject: Feature request: Bulk export for project data

comments.content: I'd like to request a new feature for your software. Our team frequently needs to analyze project data in external tools, but currently we have to export each project individually, which is time-consuming when working with dozens of projects. Could you add a bulk export feature that would allow us to select multiple projects and export them all at once? Ideally, this would include options for different export formats (CSV, Excel, JSON) and the ability to select which data fields to include in the export. This would save us several hours each week. Thanks for considering this request!

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Thank you for reaching out with this feature suggestion! I appreciate you taking the time to share how a bulk export capability would improve your workflow.

This is actually an excellent suggestion that would benefit many of our customers. I'm happy to submit this as a formal feature request to our product team. To help strengthen the request, could you share a bit more about:

1. Approximately how many projects you typically need to export at once
2. Which external tools you're using for analysis
3. Any specific data fields that are most important to include in these exports

This additional context will help our team better understand your needs and prioritize the feature appropriately.

2. We primarily use Power BI and Tableau for visualizations, and occasionally Python/Pandas for more complex analysis

3. The most critical fields are project timelines, resource allocations, budget data, and completion percentages. Being able to select these fields rather than exporting everything would also save us time in data cleanup.

If it helps, we'd be happy to participate in any beta testing for this feature when it becomes available.

In the meantime, would a workaround be useful to you? We do have an API that allows for programmatic export of multiple projects. comments.author: customer

The API workaround sounds interesting - we do have a couple of developers who could probably help set something up. Could you please share the documentation for that? Even a temporary solution would help us in the short term.

comments.author: agent

I'm happy to help with the API documentation! We updated to version 5.8 last night, and this morning none of our staff can access ANY transaction records from before January 2023. This is ABSOLUTELY UNACCEPTABLE! We run financial reports DAILY and need immediate access to our historical data. This is costing us thousands of dollars in lost productivity. We need this fixed IMMEDIATELY or we will be forced to look for another solution. I expect a call from someone in the next hour with a resolution.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I sincerely apologize for this severe issue you're experiencing after the v5.8 update. I understand the critical nature of your historical transaction data and the significant impact this is having on your business operations.

I want to assure you that we're treating this with the highest priority. I've already escalated this to our senior technical team, and they're investigating the issue right now. The good news is that all your historical data is still intact in our secure database - this appears to be an access issue rather than data loss.

Could you please provide these additional details to help us troubleshoot faster:

comments.author: agent

The v5.8 update included a new query timeout parameter that was incorrectly applied to historical data queries. This is affecting all customers who have more than 12 months of transaction history.

We're implementing an emergency patch (v5.8.1) right now to correct this issue. Rather than waiting for you to install the update, our team can apply it directly to your instance remotely, which would be the fastest resolution. We can have this completed within the next 30 minutes.

Alternatively, there is an immediate workaround: you can temporarily restore access by modifying a configuration setting:
1. Go to System Admin > Configuration > Query Parameters

3. Save and restart the application service

Would you prefer we apply the emergency patch remotely, or would you like to try the workaround while waiting for the official patch?

conversations.subject: Integration with third-party CRM not working correctly

comments.author: customer
comments.content: Hello, we're having issues with the integration between your platform and our Salesforce CRM. We set up the integration last week using your documentation, and while the initial sync seemed to work, we're noticing that customer data updated in Salesforce isn't being reflected in your system, even after 24+ hours. The documentation says updates should sync within an hour. We've checked our API limits and we're well under the threshold. Can you help us troubleshoot this issue?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Hi there! Thank you for reaching out about this integration issue. I'd be happy to help troubleshoot why the updates from Salesforce aren't syncing to our platform as expected.

Could you please provide a few additional details to help me investigate:

1. Which Salesforce edition are you using (Enterprise, Professional, etc.)?
2. What version of our integration connector do you have installed? (You can find this in Settings > Integrations > Salesforce)
3. Are all updates failing to sync, or only specific types of data?
4. Have you made any customizations to the standard Salesforce fields that you're trying to sync?

Once I have this information, I'll be able to better diagnose what might be happening.

comments.author: customer
comments.content: We're using Salesforce Enterprise Edition (Version Winter '23). The connector version is 3.5.2 according to our settings page. It seems like contact information updates (phone numbers, email addresses, etc.) are syncing fine, but any updates to opportunity status, custom fields, or account ownership aren't coming through. We do have some custom fields in Salesforce, but we mapped them according to your documentation using the field mapping tool in the integration settings.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Thank you for providing those details. Based on what you've described, I think I know what might be happening. There are a couple of potential issues we should check:

1. Connector version 3.5.2 has a known issue with syncing opportunity status changes and account ownership transfers specifically. We released version 3.5.4 last month that fixes this issue.

2. For custom fields, there's an additional step needed beyond the field mapping tool - you need to enable the "Custom Object Sync" option in the Advanced Settings tab of the integration configuration.

I recommend updating the connector to the latest version (3.5.4) first, as this will likely resolve the opportunity and account ownership sync issues. After updating, we can check if the custom fields start syncing correctly, or if we need to adjust the Advanced Settings.

Would you like me to guide you through the update process, or would you prefer to follow our documentation to perform the update?

comments.author: customer
comments.content: I wasn't aware that we weren't on the latest version of the connector. That's frustrating - we just set this up last week following your documentation, which didn't mention anything about a newer version being available. I'll try updating to 3.5.4 now, but can you also point me to where the "Custom Object Sync" setting is? I don't see it in the Advanced Settings tab - maybe it's labeled differently in our version?

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I apologize for the confusion and frustration. You're right - if you set this up last week, our documentation should have directed you to the latest version. I'll make sure our team updates the documentation immediately.

Regarding the Custom Object Sync setting - in version 3.5.2, it's actually labeled as "Extended Field Synchronization" and is located under Advanced Settings > Data Synchronization Options. It's been renamed to "Custom Object Sync" in version 3.5.4 for clarity.

After you update the connector, the setting will appear with the new name in a more prominent location. The update process should preserve your existing field mappings, but I recommend taking a screenshot of your current configuration just in case.

If you encounter any issues during the update, please let me know immediately. The update process typically takes about 5-10 minutes, during which time synchronization will be paused.

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
I've updated to version 3.5.4 and found the Custom Object Sync option - you're right, it's much easier to find now. I've enabled it and initiated a manual sync. I'll monitor it over the next few hours to see if the issues are resolved. 

One question though - will this trigger a full re-sync of all our data, or will it just sync the changes that were missed? We have a lot of records and I'm concerned about hitting API limits if it's going to sync everything again.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I'm glad you were able to update successfully and locate the Custom Object Sync option! 

To answer your question: enabling the Custom Object Sync will only trigger a sync of the custom objects and fields specifically, not a complete data re-sync. The connector is designed to be intelligent about this - it will only process records that have been updated since the last successful sync, as well as any records that use the custom fields you've mapped.

Regarding API limits, the connector includes rate limiting controls to ensure you don't hit Salesforce's API limits. By default, it will pace the requests to stay under 80% of your hourly API call limit. You can adjust this in Settings > Integrations > Salesforce > Advanced > API Utilization if needed.

Please let me know how the sync goes over the next few hours. If you notice any issues or have additional questions, I'll be here to help!

comments.author: customer
comments.content:
Good news - after the update and enabling Custom Object Sync, everything is working correctly now. Our opportunity data and custom fields are syncing properly. Thanks for your help in resolving this.

One suggestion: it would be really helpful if your product had some kind of notification system for critical connector updates. We wouldn't have known about this issue if we hadn't manually checked why things weren't syncing. Maybe an email alert when a new connector version addresses major bugs?
